group_assessment.weighting: A narrative review of CRH, ACTH and glucocorticoids in epilepsy with no methods section, no search strategy and no appraisal; language assistance by machine translation is acknowledged. Much of it rests on rodent models and small human studies. WWOX does not appear in the text. Useful only as background on why the adrenal axis and ACTH/steroid therapy are mechanistically entangled with seizures.

entries.proposition: The review states no search strategy; the Introduction states the aim as a literature review.
entries.snippet: This article presents the intrinsic relationships of CRH, ACTH, and GCs in the HPA axis as an important regulatory pathway with epilepsy through a literature review

entries.proposition: Machine translation tools were used for language assistance.
entries.snippet: as well as to Baidu Translator and other software for their assistance

entries.proposition: CRH and CRHR1 expression is reported higher in tissue from infantile spasms patients than in control tissue.
entries.snippet: The expression levels of CRH and CRHR1 were significantly higher in the epileptogenic tissues of patients with infantile spasms than in normal control tissues

entries.proposition: ACTH acts on the adrenal cortex to drive conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone and cortisol synthesis.
entries.snippet: promoting the conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone via the AC-cAMP-PKA and PLC-IP3/DG-PKC pathways, thereby increasing cortisol synthesis

entries.proposition: The HPA axis is described as largely under GABAergic control, with impaired GABAergic control proposed to cause HPA hyperexcitability.
entries.snippet: The HPA axis mediated by the organism’s stress response is largely under GABAergic control, and impaired GABAergic control may lead to hyperexcitability of the HPA axis and increased susceptibility to future seizures.

entries.proposition: ACTH is called the preferred short-term option for infantile spasms, with no significant difference from prednisolone reported.
entries.snippet: studies have found no significant difference between the effects of ACTH and prednisolone treatments for infantile spasms

entries.proposition: Glucocorticoids are described as bidirectional in epilepsy: both GR activation (antiepileptic) and chronic excess (pro-epileptogenic) are reported.
entries.snippet: GCs play a bidirectional role in the treatment of epilepsy.

entries.proposition: Seizures activate the HPA axis, and the review frames the relation as circular.
entries.snippet: In short, seizures can lead to dysregulation of the HPA axis that, in turn, can promote seizures.

entries.proposition: Mutations in the ACTH receptor (melanocortin 2 receptor) are cited as a cause of familial glucocorticoid deficiency with seizures.
entries.snippet: Mutations in the ACTH receptor (melanocortin 2 receptor) cause type-1 FGD, which can manifest as low serum cortisol levels, high ACTH levels, and seizures.
